verses.text: If I speak in the languages of people and of angels, but do not have love, I am only a noisy gong or a clanging cymbal.
If I have the gift of speaking God's message, and understand all secrets and all knowledge, and if I have enough faith to move mountains, but do not have love, I am nothing.
If I give away everything I own to feed the poor, and even give up my body to be burned, but do not have love, I gain nothing.
Love is patient. Love is kind. Love is not jealous. It does not boast. It is not proud.
It is not rude. It does not look out only for itself. It is not easily angered. It does not keep a record of wrongs.
Love is not happy with evil, but is happy with the truth.
Love always protects, always trusts, always hopes, and always keeps going.
Love never ends. But the gift of speaking God's message will come to an end. The gift of speaking in other languages will stop. Knowledge will pass away.
For now we know only in part, and we speak God's message only in part.
But when what is complete comes, what is only in part will pass away.
When I was a child, I talked like a child. I felt like a child, and I thought like a child. When I became a man, I put childish ways behind me.
Now we see only a dim picture, as in a mirror. But then we will see face to face. Now I know only in part. Then I will know fully, just as God knows me fully.
So now these three remain: faith, hope and love. But the greatest of these is love.
